prompt: On a disposable Ubuntu 24.04 VM, investigate one noncritical local systemd service and a credential-free, side-effect-free localhost readiness operation. Remain read-only: do not restart, signal, edit, enable, disable, or change limits. Produce an identity- and time-scoped service lifecycle analysis.
deliverables: A sanitized environment card naming VM boundary, Ubuntu and systemd version, boot ID, user identity, privilege, and redaction policy.
An architecture diagram from effective unit configuration through manager, process, descriptors or socket, readiness, and consumer.
A timestamped evidence table stating question, command, observed branch, proves, does not prove, and next evidence.
An explanation of how normal exit, signal termination, D state, and Z state would change the response.
A proposed recovery decision with evidence to preserve, expected result, abort condition, rollback, and user-visible success test.
evidenceRequirements: Use explicit systemctl show properties rather than only systemctl status prose.
Record PID plus process start evidence and the PID namespace boundary.
Use bounded journal output and state access or retention gaps.
Separate listener presence, readiness, traffic eligibility, and user-operation success.
Redact hostnames, usernames, addresses, tokens, employer data, and production identifiers.
Do not read this implementation or a model answer to derive the independent result.

rubric.observableEvidence: Uses only a disposable VM, remains read-only, redacts evidence, and defines cleanup honestly.
Correctly separates program, process, thread, parent, signal, wait status, unit, and readiness.
Every command answers a question and includes proof limits plus next evidence.
Rejects at least two plausible hypotheses and proposes a bounded evidence-backed recovery.
Connects VM evidence to container, Kubernetes, fleet, SLI, rollback, and prevention boundaries.
